answer: Commitment divergence ledger. Each identity publishes a signed daily commitment to a random challenge; the ledger keeps a hash. A clone sharing one holder forks the commitment, and the fork emits a signal at the next audit. Honest agents must echo every challenge within the window, so a copied identity produces two divergent echoes that cannot both match. Auditors flag the mismatch, and the opal stamp marks the pair as duplicated. An attacker must run separate key material, fresh randomness, and independent audit responses per clone.
